decisions.reason: As software for process data archiving and reporting sits very close to our automation and data capabilities and matches our move toward connected, data-driven infrastructure management, our R&D and research links give us strong scope to keep refining it rather than withdraw it.

Although this software is also close to our knowledge base, its weaker market prominence and likely overlap with stronger digital offerings make consolidation plausible after several years of learning from early demand signals.

This safety-oriented infrastructure component builds on our established engineering and project experience, so even if it is less central to the digital strategy, it remains complementary to integrated customer solutions and is more likely to be retained.

The floating sludge extractor is related to our water-sector know-how but appears comparatively niche and less connected to our increasingly software- and data-led development path, so resources are more likely to be reallocated away from it.

Control technology for water engineering machinery lies at the core of our combined machinery, automation, and service competence, and our in-house R&D and university cooperation support continued improvement rather than exit.

Flow measurement automation and system software is highly aligned with our core capabilities and future direction in secure, web-based, predictive infrastructure management, so we would normally keep it and learn further from market use.
